title: Proofpoint launches agent-intent security platform linking AI actions to data access
subtitle: The Proofpoint Agentic Data and AI Security system runs three autonomous security agents — detection, investigation, remediation — and ties each agent action to the data it touched, aimed at enterprises where AI assistants have already moved past pilot.
author: AESOP AI Engine
body: Proofpoint announced its Agentic Data and AI Security system on September 22, 2026 — a single product that links agent intent with the specific data an agent accesses and runs three autonomous security agents to spot and act on risky agent behavior in real time. A detection agent treats intent and access as one signal. An investigation agent reconstructs what happened across data, identity, and behavior automatically. A remediation agent turns that understanding into action through access changes and DLP policy optimization. Capabilities in the system, along with Semantic Business Policies and Agentic Insights, are expected to be generally available by year-end 2026.

The architectural bet is that enterprise agents will proliferate faster than manual policy can keep up, so the security layer itself has to be agentic. Proofpoint's own 2026 AI and Human Risk Landscape report found that 87% of organizations had moved AI assistants beyond pilot programs, while 52% were not confident their controls could detect a compromise. Detection watches for anomalous agent tool-use patterns, investigation reconstructs the intent chain that led to a flagged action, and remediation can revoke tokens, quarantine data, or halt an agent workflow before it completes. The three agents compress what a human SOC analyst would do into a loop that runs at machine speed.

This lands three weeks after CISA and NSA added several LiteLLM MCP auth-bypass CVEs to the Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog, and the same day Cisco Talos disclosed CLOSEDQUORUM — the first fully autonomous AI-controlled malware. Enterprise security vendors — Proofpoint, CrowdStrike, Palo Alto, Lasso, Anaconda (via the Enkrypt acquisition) — are converging on the same product shape: an agent-aware policy engine layered on top of existing DLP and identity infrastructure. Expect a wave of Q4 launches in this category.

Takeaway for learners — if you are evaluating agent frameworks for a real deployment in 2026, watching the agent is now a distinct engineering decision, not something inherited from your identity provider. The interesting design choice is whether monitoring runs in-line (blocking, higher latency, hard to bypass) or out-of-band (visibility, lower latency, easier to circumvent). Proofpoint's architecture appears to be a mix. Understanding the trade-off will make you more useful to any team putting agents into production.
